title: Name judged parts by content, not position
statement: Name each judged part by what it is rather than by its position, so its judgments can be compared across drafts.
example: In one remade glossary a redraft inserted one term, so every id from 4 to 9 named a different term in the two drafts.
detail: The glossary's judge state names each entry by its position, term_0, line_0 and note_0 onwards. In one remade glossary the second draft inserted a term at id 4, so every id from 4 to 9 named a different term in the two drafts: three glosses identical in term, line and note moved to new ids, and a fourth moved with a shortened note. Comparing or replaying judgments by id across those drafts compares different words.
against: Within one draft the ids are unambiguous, and the whole state is logged, so content can be matched again by hand.
